# M04 — Regime detection (Phase 4)

*Generated by `python -m src.experiments.run_regimes` on 2026-07-18 17:47 UTC. Numbers trace to `results/tables/m04_regimes_*` and `results/predictions/m04_regimes_*.parquet`.*

## Scope

Roadmap Phase 4 (Ch2 §2.4): detect latent **volatility regimes** on S&P 500 daily data with the two pre-registered estimators — a Gaussian-emission **HMM** (Baum–Welch; Hamilton 1989) and the **Nystrup, Lindström & Madsen (2020) jump model** — both on *standardised daily log returns*. Regimes are the discrete state the Phase-5 LSTM conditions on; this phase characterises and validates them, and builds the **leakage-free causal posterior** that Phase 5 will consume.

- **Sample:** 2000-02-03 → 2022-02-25 (5530 trading days), target `intraday_2019_2022`.
- **Emission features:** `['ret']` (standardised).
- **Headline K = 3** (calm / transitional / crisis), the interpretable choice (Guidolin 2011; Ch2 §2.4); BIC sensitivity below.

## Model selection — BIC by K

| K | HMM logL | HMM params | HMM BIC | Jump logL | Jump params | Jump BIC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | -6623.3 | 7 | 13306.9 | -6835.6 | 4 | 13705.7 |
| 3 | -6349.8 | 14 | 12820.2 | -6592.9 | 6 | 13237.4 |
| 4 | -6313.4 | 23 | 12825.0 | -6552.8 | 8 | 13174.6 |

BIC prefers **K=3** (HMM) / **K=4** (jump). The headline map fixes **K=3** for interpretability (calm/transitional/crisis); Chapter 2 §2.4 pre-commits to a small, interpretable state space over BIC-chasing on the modest samples of daily data.

## Persistence

| state | label | stay prob | expected duration (days) | stationary | freq | mean run (days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | calm | 0.976 | 40.9 | 0.479 | 0.494 | 68.3 |
| 1 | transitional | 0.966 | 29.0 | 0.434 | 0.427 | 45.4 |
| 2 | crisis | 0.961 | 25.8 | 0.087 | 0.079 | 39.8 |

![transition matrix](../figures/m04/intraday_2019_2022_transition.png)

The jump penalty λ is **tuned, not fixed** (Ch2 §2.4; Nystrup 2020): the headline map uses λ=**3** — the smallest penalty on the sweep meeting the persistence floor. Full λ sensitivity is in `results/tables/m04_regimes_intraday_2019_2022_jump_lambda.csv`.

## External validation — VIX by regime

Mean VIX rises monotonically with the (volatility-ordered) regime index — the unsupervised states line up with market-implied volatility without ever seeing it:

| state | calm | transitional | crisis |
|---|---|---|---|
| mean VIX | 14.5 | 22.4 | 40.5 |

Rank concordance (Spearman) between state and VIX = **0.789**; state/VIX-quantile diagonal concordance = **0.566**.


![VIX by state](../figures/m04/intraday_2019_2022_vix_by_state.png)

## Estimator robustness — HMM vs jump model

The two estimators agree on **97.4%** of days (adjusted Rand 0.921). The jump model, by penalising transitions, yields the more persistent sequence — the property Nystrup et al. (2020) motivate as the remedy for the HMM's state-switching noise (Ch2 §2.4).

## Leakage discipline — smoothed vs causal-filtered posterior

The regime *map* above uses the **smoothed** posterior P(sₜ | x₁..x_T), the right tool to describe which regime was active historically (Ch2 §2.4). A forecast, however, may only use the **filtered** posterior P(sₜ | x₁..xₜ), which conditions on the past alone. Fitting the HMM on the **training split only** (≤ 2015-12-31) and filtering causally over the test window, the mean absolute gap between the smoothed and filtered crisis probability is **0.034** — concentrated, as expected, around turning points, where the smoother's hindsight matters most.


![smoothed vs filtered](../figures/m04/intraday_2019_2022_smoothed_vs_filtered.png)

> **Phase-5 hand-off / Ch3 note.** Chapter 2 §2.5 currently describes passing the *smoothed* state probabilities to the LSTM. Taken literally over the full sample, that would leak the future into an out-of-sample forecast. The leakage-free realisation — and what the persisted `hmm_filt_p*` columns hold — is the **causal filtered** posterior from a train-fit HMM (refit as the walk-forward expands), lagged one day. Recommend reconciling the Chapter 3 wording to 'filtered (causal) state probabilities' accordingly.

- **Tables:** `results/tables/m04_regimes_intraday_2019_2022_{bic,persistence,vix_confusion,jump_lambda,agreement}.csv`.

## Gate criteria

- [x] Gaussian-emission HMM on standardised daily log returns (Baum–Welch, restarts).

- [x] Nystrup et al. (2020) jump-penalised estimator; λ tuned via a persistence sweep.

- [x] K∈{2,3,4} compared by BIC; interpretable K=3 headline (calm/transitional/crisis).

- [x] Persistence statistics (transition matrix, expected durations).

- [x] External validation against VIX quantiles (confusion + rank concordance).

- [x] Volatility-ordered states; HMM↔jump agreement reported.

- [x] Leakage-free causal filtered posterior built + demonstrated for Phase 5.
